answer: We formalize a consensus model where a cryptographic pulse synchronizes zero-knowledge verifiable delays, ensuring that validators who wander from the protocol suffer execution lag. By securing each identity with staking collateral S bound to subgame-perfect slashing penalties exceeding the maximum attack payoff, even a coordinated whisper of collusion yields strictly negative expected utility. Therefore, dynamic opportunity-cost bonds guarantee that identity multiplication is strictly dominated, converging to a unique and robust Nash equilibrium.
